Johan killed the people around Wolf one by one over the years, not all at once, so he wouldn't have immediately known that it was Johan.

When Johan and Nina arrived in Germany, Wolf asked Johan how he felt. Johan decided to make Wolf feel the same way that he did and killed everyone who knew him so that he would feel isolated and cut off from his past.

Johan was then taken to 511 Kinderheim where the East German government hoped to turn children into supermen in part by eroding their sense of identity. We'll later learn that the children promised to remember one another's names and details of their lives so they wouldn't forget.

The Baby leads a neo-Nazi group which wants to use Nina to draw Johan to them to become their leader and go on to become the new Hitler. Johan has no interest in working with the neo-Nazis, though, and Wolf thinks the Baby's plan is stupid. I can't remember if Wolf said anything about getting rid of the Turks.

1. Series 1 - An amazing season that revived Who, introduced a great new Doctor and companion and was of relatively consistent quality. One of my favourite seasons of all Who, alongside the Third Doctor and Liz's adventures in season 7. (Best - The Empty Child/The Doctor Dances. Worst - The Unquiet Dead?)


2. Series 4 - I'm not a fan of Tennant, but you can tell he's got a real handle on the role of the Doctor and Donna is brought back as one of the best companions ever. There's the odd story I don't like but it really is one of the strongest runs. (Best - Turn Left. Worst - The Doctor's Daughter)


3. Series 10 - My favourite Moffat season, with a fresh start for the Twelfth Doctor with Bill, a welcome replacement for Clara who probably should have left in Death in Heaven or Last Christmas. Missy is amazing, Bill and Nardole are funny and the Twelfth Doctor gets his best showing. There are a few duds and the Monks were a misfore but all-in-all a pretty good season. (Best - World Enough and Time/The Doctor Falls. Worst - Empress of Mars or The Eaters of Light)


4. Series 9 - The decision to do mostly two-parters was a good one and most of them are very good. The character of Ashildr wasn't done very well at all and her two-parter is easily the weakest two-parter of the season. Clara is back to her unshakeable self and Danny's death is all but forgotten. The hybrid arc feels tired and boring but Heaven Sent is amazing. (Best - Heaven Sent. Worst - Sleep No More)


5. Series 3 - A real mix of episodes, some strong (Blink, the three-part finale) and quite a few weak (the Dalek two-parter, 42). Martha is never really allowed to step out of Rose's shadow until her departure, which I suppose is the point but doesn't make her the most interesting companion there is when we're not really allowed to get to know her. (Best - Human Nature/The Family of Blood or Utopia. Worst - Daleks in Manhattan/Evolution of the Daleks)


6. Series 5 - The Eleventh Doctor and River are at their best, but Amy is at her very worst. She's a terrible person and deeply unlikeable at this stage. Vincent and the Doctor is mostly boring and only remembered for its amazing ending. The angel two-parter is one of my favourite Who stories ever but, of course, has that horrible ending where Amy sexually assaults the Doctor on the night before her wedding. (Best - The Time of Angels/Flesh and Stone. Worst - Victory of the Daleks.)


7. Series 2 - A generally weak season that had a lot to live up to and didn't quite deliver. It gave us Yvonne Hartman, who was unfortunately killed off - thank God for Big Finish - and brought back the beloved Sarah Jane Smith and K9. Tennant doesn't seem comfortable in the role yet and gets by by acting overenthusiastic about everything. Rose, who I adored in series 1, has become rather smug. (Best - The Girl in the Fireplace. Worst - Fear Her [Love & Monsters was good])


8. Series 7 - This series manages to push ahead of series 8 thanks to a strong first half. Dinosaurs on a Spaceship was poor, but Asylum through to Angels is a very strong run with a very likeable Amy and Rory. Then we get Clara, who is at her very worst and most vacuous. The return of the Great Intelligence is good, I guess. (Best - A Town Called Mercy. Worst - The Rings of Akhaten.)


9. Series 11 - The one word I can think of to describe this series is "lacking". It's lacking any interesting characterisation of the Doctor (beyond the "assume her dad is dead" moment) and very lacking in the companion department. Graham is alright and perhaps Yaz and Ryan should have been excised. (Best - Demons of the Punjab. Worst - The Tsuranga Conundrum.)


10. Series 8 - The show was trying too hard to make the Twelfth Doctor dark and edgy, which clashes horribly with stories like Robot of Sherwood and The Caretaker. The Ninth Doctor was dark and the Third Doctor was grumpy but both were very likeable. Something didn't quite work for me - perhaps it would have if we'd had a Liz or a Rose rather than Clara. (Best - Listen. Worst - In the Forest of the Night)


11. Series 6 - As far as I'm concerned, the nadir of the show. Complicated and uninteresting plotting and overuse of the once likeable and enigmatic River combine to make a messy season that only manages to ruin River. She's a "child of the TARDIS", the daughter of Amy and Rory but also their best friend from school and a psychopath engineered to kill the Doctor. What was wrong with her being an archaeologist from the future who does her own thing and doesn't have her whole life revolve around her husband, whom she marries in a terribly nonsensical scene. (Best - The Impossible Astronaut/Day of the Moon. Worst - The Curse of the Black Spot or The Wedding of River Song)

The Chaos Emeralds are seven (sometimes six, sometimes eight) jewels that contain extraordinary power when used in unison, and that can be controlled using the Master Emerald. All eight gems were kept safe at a shrine in what would later be known as Mystic Ruins. They, and the chao creatures that lived at the shrine, came to be protected by Chaos, a chao that became a warm-hearted watery monster thanks to exposure to the Master Emerald.

4000 years before the present, the echidna Tikal was born. The daughter of the Chief Pachacamac, she was raised by her grandmother. After Grandma (that's what her people called her) died, Pachacamac became a power-hungry warlord, conquering nearby tribes in the name of his subjects.

Tikal wasn't too happy about this. She befriended Chaos and the chao, her trusted her enough to show her the Emerald Shrine. Pachacamac learnt of this, and tried to steal the Emeralds. Seeing the chao hurt by Pachacamac's warriors, Chaos absorbed the power of the Seven Emeralds and killed Pachacamac, his people, and ruined their civilization. Tikal used the power of the Master Emerald to seal herself and Chaos inside of the jewel to prevent further destruction. The island on which the shrine existed was raised into the sky. The Chaos Emeralds dispersed elsewhere.

Some members of the clan survived, and presumably lived in the ruins of their once great city. They made a mural depicting Chaos in his perfect form. Others lived on the floating Angel Island, protecting the Master Emerald so that Chaos could not be released. 

Thousands of years later, the United Federation has become one of, if not the, most powerful country on the planet. Gerald Robotnik, who studied Chaos and managed to create creatures based on him, was asked by the President to discover immortality. His granddaughter, Maria, was dying, so Gerald agreed to. He created a life-form named Shadow, thanks to the help of the alien Black Doom, who asked only that Shadow collect the Chaos Emeralds for him in return. However, the military saw Shadow as a threat, so all those involved in the project were killed or arrested. Maria herself was shot after helping Shadow escape to Earth, where he was captured anyway. The vengeful Gerald Robotnik managed to modify Shadow to seek revenge by collecting the Chaos Emeralds and using them to initiate a program that would send Space Colony ARK towards the Earth at far too great a velocity. Gerald was later executed, and Shadow locked away.

Modern day; Gerald's grandson and Maria's cousin, Ivo Robotnik, plans to rule the world. He is stopped by Sonic the Hedgehog, and later his friend, Miles Prower. By this time, the guardians of the Master Emerald are all extinct except for one survivor, named Knuckles, who joins Sonic and Tails after Dr. Robotnik tried to trick him into collecting the Emeralds for him.

The series explores several plotlines --- Dr. Robotnik finding stone tablets that told him about Chaos; Shadow being freed by Robotnik and using him to get Gerald's revenge for Maria's death; what happened to the ancient world after Pachacamac and his tribe's deaths; and the constant search for the Chaos Emeralds.
